note: Aliases are pure sugar: they resolve to canonical IRIs BEFORE a claim is built, so the signed wire form always carries the full IRI. This file is content-addressed and federates like any record; a consumer may remap it. An alias binding is itself expressible as a signed owl:sameAs claim. Vocabulary policy (normative: the protocol spec/vocabulary.md; rationale: DECISIONS §20/§21): reuse a PUBLISHED ontology wherever one fits (PROV, PAV, DCAT, OWL, SKOS, schema.org - e.g. schema:AcceptAction/RejectAction for a review verdict - and the W3C Security Vocabulary sec: for key->principal control, a signed key binding being a lightweight Verifiable Credential); mint kton-native IRIs (nk:) only for concepts no standard covers; and RESERVE the qa: terms for a quality process that actually keeps records. NOTE (2026-09-16): the `reviewed` alias below resolves to pav:reviewedBy, and PAV HAS NO SUCH PROPERTY - its 33 terms are authoredBy, createdBy, curatedBy, importedBy, retrievedBy, contributedBy and the rest, verified against the published ontology, not recalled. There is no established property for `reviewed by`; the replacement is being decided in the kton spec and this alias is wrong until it lands. A reused vocabulary is a claim about somebody else's document, so it has to be looked up.
